question: Which Article of the Constitution of India deals with the Conduct of Business of the Government of a State?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 166**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 166** of the Constitution of India deals with **"Conduct of Business of the Government of a State**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Part VI of the Constitution** deals with the government in the states.
 
• **Articles 153 to 167** in Part VI of the Constitution deal with the **state executive.**

Some important articles under this part include the following:

 
 

 
 
**Article 163**

 
 
 
 
• There shall be a **council of ministers with the chief minister as the head** to aid and advice the governor
 
 
 
 

 
 
**Article 164**

 
 
 
 
• The chief minister is appointed by the governor
 
• Other ministers are appointed by the governor on the advice of the chief minister
 
• Ministers shall hold the office during the pleasure of the governor
 
 
 
 

 
 
**Article 166**

 
 
 
 
• **Conduct of business of the government of a state.**
 
 
 
 

 
 
**Article 167**

 
 
 
Duties of chief minister

 
 
• To communicate between the governor of the state of the council of ministers
 
• To furnish information relating to the administration of affairs of state to the governor
